archiveTitle: Morning Brief | How to Fish surpasses 1 million players in two days

entries.headline: Developer announces 1 million players within two days of launch
entries.summary: Dazed Games announced in an official Steam news post that cooperative fishing game How to Fish has reached 1 million players within two days of release. The Steam store confirms the game launched on August 20 and supports 1–4 player co-op; this official milestone indicates it quickly became an indie hit over its first weekend.
entries.verification: Opened the specific Steam official announcement page, Steam store, and the specific Denfaminicogamer report; the official announcement title directly confirms '1 million in two days,' and the store verifies developer, release date, and platform.
entries.timeNote: The developer's Steam announcement was published within this window; Denfaminicogamer reported at 07:28 Beijing time and linked to the official announcement.

entries.headline: Moon Studios head says current Ori 3 development rumors are 'unfounded'
entries.summary: In response to NateTheHate's claim that a new Ori is being developed by a team under Saber Interactive, Moon Studios head Thomas Mahler stated in a public post that he is unaware of such a project and further called current Ori 3 rumors unfounded; he also revealed that the team has internally discussed buying back the IP from Microsoft. Since neither Microsoft nor Saber has commented on project status, this entry only confirms Mahler's denial and does not assert that no related project exists within Microsoft.
entries.verification: Opened the specific TrueGaming report and verified the embedded Mahler original post, account, and date; 3DM relayed the same public statement. The original X page was not directly opened, so it is not marked official; Microsoft and Saber have not confirmed project status.
entries.timeNote: Mahler's original post is dated August 23; Russian media published a relay at 02:46 Beijing time, and Arabic media later embedded the original post. This entry records the earliest verifiable report time.

entries.headline: Addendum: Revenue up 10%, but net loss widens to ¥22.243 billion
entries.summary: Based on SNK's 25th fiscal period disclosure, gamebiz reports revenue of ¥5.715 billion for the December 2025 period, up 10% year-on-year, with an operating loss of ¥19.901 billion and a net loss of ¥22.243 billion; the company also borrowed $40 million from its parent company at an annual interest rate of 7.28%, with a lump-sum repayment due in October 2029. This information was originally intended for the August 21 evening brief but was missed during that search; it is now included as an addendum.
entries.verification: Opened the specific gamebiz financial report and verified revenue, three loss figures, loan amount, interest rate, and maturity date; AUTOMATON WEST and 3DM both point back to the same disclosure and are not treated as independent primary financial reports. SNK's original financial documents were not obtained, so it is marked media_report and noted as an addendum.
entries.timeNote: The original report time was 11:19 Japan time on August 21, i.e., 10:19 Beijing time, which falls within the 2026-08-21 evening window; it is added here due to an earlier industry search omission.

entries.headline: Final session enters opening window at 10:00 Beijing time per official schedule
entries.summary: The official schedule for The Duskbloods network test lists the fifth session as 11:00–15:00 Japan time on August 24, i.e., 10:00–14:00 Beijing time. As of the 10:10 cutoff, the session has entered its scheduled opening window; however, no official status post has been obtained, so this entry only confirms the schedule and time, and does not infer server stability or player accessibility.
entries.verification: Opened the official network test special page and the specific Famitsu schedule page, verifying the fifth session's Japan time and Beijing time conversion. No accessible live server status announcement exists, so the report is limited to 'entering the opening window per schedule' and does not confirm actual service status.
entries.timeNote: 11:00 Japan time converts to 10:00 Beijing time, which falls within this window and before the 10:10 cutoff.
